suggested_requirements.text: The system shall track the movement of lapsed quantities in an area including the permit and well, location, reason, and MFL zone.
The system shall track the relocation of active water use within the SWUCA.
The system shall report on the history of irrigation water conserving credits including balance, earned, used, and drought quantities.
The system shall track and report on the history of permitted data including use type, irrigated acres, and pumpage.
The system shall track and measure alternative source projects including surface water, reclaimed water, augmented surface water, ASR, desalination, and conservation.
The system shall display the spatial impact of an application with other active applications on-line.
The system shall create a heat map indicating over-pumping status and water quality.
The system shall report on permits that have been relocated by a permit holder.
The system shall track the impact that water use has on set MFL levels.
The system shall track net benefit changes including relocated permits, change of use, locations, lapsed quantities, reclaimed water, and projects.
The system shall report the net benefit amount in MGD for changes in location, use, land use, lapsed quantities, and water withdrawal credit.
The system shall mark permits that have a land use change for potential relocation to public supply utility.
The system shall create a layer that includes cones of depression for MFL information.
The system shall report on water use amounts sold or given from one permit to another.
The system shall report on the improvement percentage, location, cost, and method for mitigation of MFL impacts.
The system shall report on water made available through District water resource development projects.
The system shall report on permit duration to track expiration dates.
The system shall allow comparison to adjacent districts' GIS layers.
The system shall report compliance and crop reports on a permit level.
The system shall report on competing applications.
The system shall supply Regulatory requirements of MFL data including water levels in relationship to MFL and historic/current levels.
The system shall determine the availability of alternative use supplies.
The system shall report the Reservation from use amounts allocated to participants.
The system shall track ownership of wells or permits over the life of the withdrawal point.
The system shall display permitted quantities, actual pumpage, and resource usage.
The system shall track requested and permitted quantities.
The system shall identify when a standby permit is reactivated due to loss of alternative quantities.
The system shall generate a heat map showing permit information for specific time periods and geographic areas.
The system shall allow public utilities and internal staff to find existing permits in or near their service area.
The system shall analyze permits using a soils type GIS layer.
The system shall provide printable and customizable maps.
The system shall identify when the District or another governmental agency purchases land to show if there is a permit to be retired.
The system shall track how water use changes when land use changes.
The system shall allow querying data by issue date, expiration date, use type, predominate use, pumpage reports, permitted quantities, and permit status.
The system shall generate a well package providing a view of water use at a particular time for model input.
The system shall associate permitted quantities, pumpage quantities, and use code data at the well level.
The system shall track changes in land use and its effect on water availability.
The system shall provide historical data for Water Use Permits including spatial representations.
The system shall track trends in land use and water use changes.
The system shall track water use over time and negotiate new water use based on pumpage trends.
